about.bio:
Bel Parker trained in physical theatre, mask and movement at L’École Internationale de Théâtre Jacques Lecoq in Paris, and in clown and bouffon with Philippe Gaulier.

From 2021 to 2024 Bel was Associate Director of The Big House, an award-winning company using theatre and film to transform the lives of care leavers, directing Hansel and Gretel and CashMoney Now there and later the short film Duvet. Bel now freelance directs, while managing the ViBrent programme for Punchdrunk Enrichment.

She holds a first-class degree in Arabic from SOAS, and speaks English, French, Arabic and Spanish.
about.statement:
The weird, the surprising and the magical: they’re what excite me. I look for them. I aim to nurture playfulness and curiosity in myself and those around me.

A proud jack of all trades. I love bringing together seemingly disparate interests and ideas to make something cohesive and beautiful.

I love words, languages. Equally, I LOVE finding the drama without/before/between them.

projects.title: Hansel and Gretel
projects.card_text: A promenade, site-specific performance about need, greed and growing up.
projects.hero_alt: Hansel and Gretel at The Big House
projects.lede: A promenade retelling of the fairy tale: a story of need, greed and growing up.
projects.body: Written by Josh Azouz for The Big House, this production followed two abandoned children through a starving land and into the woods.
projects.passage:
Once upon a time. The land was rotting and the people were hungry.

Once upon a time. The woodcutter and his wife were so very hungry that they couldn’t feed their children, Hansel and Gretel.

Once upon a time. Hansel and Gretel were abandoned in the woods.
projects.body_after: Set throughout the murky rooms of a disused frame factory, this retelling was tough and wild, funny and shocking.

projects.title: Adding Up America
projects.card_text: Monique DeBose’s funny, candid show about mixed-race identity in America, with original jazz-inspired songs.
projects.hero_alt: Adding Up America at Assembly Roxy
projects.lede: Some things just don’t add up.
projects.body:
Drawing on her own life, award-winning singer and storyteller Monique Debose tries to make sense of herself by running the numbers.

Adding Up America is an intimate, jazz-infused, storytelling show about race, identity and belonging.

After Los Angeles and New York, the show made its UK debut at Assembly Roxy for the 2026 Edinburgh Fringe, with Bel developing and directing the version for UK audience.

press.quote: “Profoundly moving, deeply resonant, and breathtakingly original.”
“The show manages to be deeply thought-provoking and fun at the same time.”
“Monique was outstanding! Masterful to take such an important topic, combine it with music, comedy and acting.”

projects.title: W*NKERS
projects.card_text: Raucous queer female jesters, from Theatre Deli to the Edinburgh and Brighton Fringes.
projects.body:
Since 2019, Bel and Jordana Belaiche have written, produced and performed W*NKERS together: bawdy, musical, audience-baiting comedy built on clown, with Bel as House White and Jordana as House Red. They have played FEMFEST at Theatre Deli, the Edinburgh Fringe, Chavenage House, Bread and Roses and The Divine.

Their 2026 run at Brighton Fringe, directed by Cecily Nash, moved through the turning year and the stages of a life, from May Day and Morris dancing to dating, weddings and death.

press.quote: Bel Parker has a fierce energy on-stage that it’s hard to look away from.
An excellent calling card for their bawdy, chaotic talents.

projects.title: CashMoney Now
projects.card_text: A breakneck tale of con artists, hackers, sugar daddies and crypto bros.
projects.hero_alt: CashMoney Now at The Big House
projects.lede: A breakneck tale of con artists, hackers, sugar daddies and crypto bros.
projects.body:
When her little sister loses everything to an online scam, Anna goes after the scammer, deep into the murkiest corners of the internet, where revenge comes with the chance of the heist of a lifetime.

Bel developed the script with writer James Fritz and directed the production for The Big House, where she was Associate Director.

press.quote: An original, well-written, well-acted and hilarious production.
press.source: Nicole V Sylvester, Afridiziak Theatre News

projects.title: Duvet
projects.card_text: A surreal horror short about coercive control. Official selection, Aesthetica Film Festival 2026.

laurels.alt: Official selection, London Breeze Film Festival 2026
Official nominee, London Art Film Awards 2026
Nominee, Hastings Rocks International Film Festival 2026

projects.lede: Duvet follows a young woman struggling to leave a coercive relationship. When the source of her comfort becomes a terrible adversary, she finds herself trapped in a desperate battle for freedom.
projects.body: Blending puppetry, comedy and horror, Duvet is an offbeat psychological drama exploring isolation and resilience.
projects.role_text: Bel developed Duvet with writer James Fritz after growing concerns about the prevalence of coercive relationships affecting the charity’s members. Bel directed the film, led filmmaking workshops for the company’s under-18 members during development, then crowdfunded the festival campaign on Greenlit, and ran the subsequent campaign with associate producer Tabitha Boyd.

quote.text: The Duvet allows us to get deep into our protagonist’s story, her struggle and her strength, quickly, with wit, and without having to see direct violence.

projects.watch: Duvet is on the festival circuit. Industry viewing links are available on request.
